data.name: Kronos
data.detailed_description:
Kronos is an Action, RPG, Indie game with lots of combats, customization and puzzle interaction. Explore the castle and its more than 30 areas and discovers his dark secrets hidden in it. More than 50 unique enemies, and 8 powerful and challenging bosses. Dozens of items for customize your hero: swords, axes, maces, bows, explosive arrows, poison arrows, rings, armor, helmets, shields...

And 33 unique talents to define your own play style. Kill enemies and loot items while leveling up. Craft useful potions, special arrows, and enchant your weapons with alchemy. Cast 20 powerful spells of Fire, Ice, Earth and Electric elements. Fireballs, Ice Nova, Stone Skin, Chain Lightning, and many more. Logical puzzles wich requires item searching and combining them to create the item you need.

Features


  • An entire castle to explore with 30+ huge areas.
  • More than 50 different enemies, and 8 powerful and challenging bosses.
  • Dozens of items for customize your hero. Swords, Axes, Maces, Bows, Arrows, Rings...
  • Level up your hero with 33 unique talents and improve every aspect of him.
  • Craft useful potions, special arrows, and enchant your weapons with alchemy.
  • Cast 20 powerful spells of Fire, Ice, Earth and Electric elements.
  • Hero Difficulty for who wants a more challenging gameplay.
  • Logical puzzles wich requires item and hint searching.
  • Puzzle solutions are random and change every new game.
  • Colorful elemental enviroments of Fire, Ice, Earth and Electric themes.
  • Epic original soundtrack by José Ramón 'Bibiki' García.

reviews.review:
[h1]Basic Information[/h1]
[b]Title:[/b]  Kronos
[b]Status:[/b]  Released
[b]Developer:[/b]  UroboroStudio 
[b]Publisher:[/b]  UroboroStudio
[b]Genre:[/b]  Role Playing Game
[b]Release Date:[/b]  3rd of February, 2017
[b]Type:[/b]  Singleplayer 

[h1]General Impression[/h1]
It’s hard for me to find redeeming points in Kronos’ favor. I usually have no such issues since most video games on Steam that I accept to review (I reject shovelware by principle) aren’t both overpriced and simplistic to the point of making browser-based “games”, noteworthy. This title made me reconsider what types of games I’m still willing to write about and even their future number since I’m starting to feel burned-out. If I were to make a tasteless pun, I’d say Kronos has been a waste of my time. Get it? Kronos, is a disambiguation of Chronos/Chronus, the personification of time in Greco-Roman mythology. No? Okay, the nerd will go sit quietly in a corner.

Seriously, though. The dev team made very few efforts in polishing their first and so far only Steam project. Doesn’t seem like a promising debut at all, guys. For starters, who thought that pricing this thing at 7 dollars/euros was a bright idea? Kronos doesn’t even offer Trading Cards at the time of this writing. Don’t even get me started on the “storyline”, since generic doesn’t manage to covey it by proper term. I’m an RPG fan. I clocked more hours on classic 2D RPGs than some gamers have spent so far just shooting their way from one CS or COD map to another. I can appreciate spartan looks if they are coupled at least by a more than decent story/setting/characters. Kronos features none of these, to the point at which you may not overlook the literal slow pacing (the protagonist never heard of running, in his life) and the fact that the many rooms and arenas just seem recycled one after another. And what kind a twisted joke would that be, the case of a role playing game in which you don’t really get to role play? No classes to choose from and definitely no dialogue or NPCs to interact with.

Weaponry, spell and foe diversity are a welcome sight, but the assets themselves are quite repetitive. Stylistically speaking, Kronos attempted minimalism, but failed. Imagine Prison Architect but with next to no charm, zooming in/out and a tenth of its asset variety. Not a pretty picture? My thoughts exactly. So what might this game have to offer that could still compel you to try it out? Some basic crafting mechanics, an inventory system and It features some puzzle segments that mercifully take your mind off the barebones combat sections. Never too hard or complex, you’ll still learn to respect any break from the same old rinse and repeat pattern of wacking melee weapons or shooting fireballs and arrows in the general direction of the enemy (and missing the target most of the time).

Buying this game only once it’s bundled seems like a sound plan while purchasing it directly from the Steam Store at its current pricing would be a tragedy. Too many alternatives to mention them here. One thing is certain: Steam Greenlight really deserves to disappear and perhaps the floodgates of gaming mediocrity on Steam shall be sealed tight once and for all.

[h1]Strong Points[/h1]
+ A few decent RPG mechanics.
+ Occasional puzzle segments.
+ Steam Achievements.

[h1]Weak Points[/h1]
- Plain graphics and sounds.
- Slow paced and repetitve.
- Overpriced, given what it offers.
- No Steam Trading Cards.

[b]Rating 45/100 [/b]
